title: Lunch Boxes Come Back
transcript: At a covered food market, six lunch stalls started serving takeaway meals in the same kind of reusable box. Customers paid a small deposit and could get it back at any participating stall. Returns were slow at first. A few regulars told us they passed the market on their way home, when most stalls had already shut. We moved the evening return point to a bakery by the entrance, where staff stayed until the last commuters came through. The bakery recorded each return on a shared sheet. That mattered because the market reimbursed the stall that refunded the customer, even when another stall had originally taken the deposit.

questions.prompt: What kept some regular customers from returning their boxes promptly?
options: The boxes had to be washed before return.
Most stalls were closed when they passed the market.
They often left their receipts at work.
The stalls handled returns only during quiet periods.
questions.answer: Most stalls were closed when they passed the market.
questions.explanation: 一些常客下班路过市场时，大部分摊位已经关门。

questions.prompt: What did the shared record help the market do?
options: Pay back the business that had issued each refund.
Estimate how many new boxes each kitchen needed.
Identify customers who regularly kept their boxes.
Calculate the income each stall earned from lunch sales.
questions.answer: Pay back the business that had issued each refund.
questions.explanation: 共享表记录每次归还，方便市场把垫付的押金补给实际办理退款的商家。
